components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[0-9]*$'
          example: '6085551023'
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            pets:
              title: Pets
              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array
              items:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
              readOnly: true
          required:
            - pets

## Summary

I implemented the create-time telephone normalization rule for `POST /api/owners`, splitting it into small single-responsibility pieces and reusing one normalization function across both.

**The rule, in two concerns:**

1. **Normalization (single source of truth)** — `util/TelephoneNormalizer.java`: a tiny stateless helper that strips every non-digit character (`replaceAll("\\D", "")`).

2. **Reject with 400 when not exactly 10 digits** — a Bean Validation constraint following the repo's existing idiom (`PetAgeValidation` on `Pet.birthDate`):
   - `rest/validation/TelephoneDigits.java` + `TelephoneDigitsValidator.java` — strips via `TelephoneNormalizer` and checks `length() == 10`.
   - Attached to the DTO field in `openapi.yml` via `x-field-extra-annotation`, and I removed the old digits-only `pattern: '^[0-9]*$'` so formatted input like `(04) 1234-5678` reaches the app instead of being rejected at binding. This routes failures through the existing `@Valid` → `MethodArgumentNotValidException` → 400 machinery.

3. **Store/return the 10-digit value** — `OwnerMapper.toOwner(OwnerFieldsDto)` (the create-only mapping path) now maps `telephone` through `TelephoneNormalizer.normalize(...)`, so the stored and returned value is the bare 10 digits. The `Owner` entity's existing `@Pattern("^[0-9]{10}$")` continues to hold post-normalization.

**Why these homes:** the validator and the mapper share one normalizer (no duplicated stripping logic); validation lives with the other REST validators; the "store normalized" step lives in the create-only mapper, so update behavior is untouched (spec says "on create"); and no catch-all controller logic was added.

**Verification:** `coreStripsToTenDigits` (`(04) 1234-5678` → stored `0412345678`) and `errorRejectsTooFewDigits` (`12345` → 400) both pass, and `./mvnw test` is `BUILD SUCCESS`.
